name: verify-loop
description: Verify Loop: one place to verify a change or claim. It writes a check that can fail, loops until the check passes, keeps the proof, and returns a fixed answer (verdict, VERIFY: line, observed rejection, gaps). Users, skills and agents can all call it. Create mode generates a project /verify skill; maintain mode keeps it honest as the app changes. Also ships feature-map (manual-only): a FEATURES.md of every feature, its entry points and traces, checked against the code and linked to VERIFY.md. And latent-audit (manual-only): a dead-code cleanup held to three stages (a snapshot that records what each command really imports, in-place deletion of only never-loaded code with every command rerun, a verdict for every suspect left). And wire-check (manual-only): is code connected to the running system? A call-trace snapshot of every way in records which functions really ran, every function nothing entered gets a classified verdict, and a component you connect is kept connected by a FEATURES.md trace and a VERIFY.md check seen red on the broken wiring. And debug-protocol (manual-only): the root cause proven both ways, the failure reproduced on demand and gone with only the cause taken out, then the tree left as it was or fixed at the cause and held by a check that fails with the cause put back. And structure-gate (manual-only): is it spaghetti, measured? The share of code a parser actually entered comes first, every region no parser entered (code in a string, a language with no parser here) gets a counted reading or UNKNOWN, every finding gets its cost, and a `no` verdict is refused over code no linter or test can reach. And threat-model (manual-only): what an attacker can make the system do, worst first. A scan counts every way in (route tables, registering decorators, handlers, scripts), each one is attacked or shown to have nothing behind it, and each attack is kept as a test the suite runs; a fix must shut every open attack and fail again with the change put back. And evolve-maintain (manual-only): change a running system without breaking it. The tree as it was is kept and the commands users and jobs run are recorded on it, every function or config line that reads a name the change touched must be entered by a recorded run or given a reason, and every recorded command must print and write on the changed tree what it did before, unless the difference is one the user asked for. And perf-optimize (manual-only): make it measurably faster. The work is timed and profiled on the code as it was at two sizes, a change is kept only when the output is the same bytes, it beats the noise and a profile pointed at what it changed, and a guard left in the suite must fail with each changed file put back. And safe-release (manual-only): deploy, or change stored data, with a proven way back. The change and its way back are rehearsed on copies of the live data with today's code and the changed code: forward and its rerun, today's code on the migrated data (the deploy window and a code-only revert), the way back compared row for row, each loss named with the step that causes it; the live data is never written. And arch-design (manual-only): could the architecture be better? Where the structure costs the user, counted, shown as before/after pictures with the chain behind each problem, the top move written out with its landing steps, proof and door, the store or seam it is not adding, and a stop to ask which move to explore before anything changes. And blast-radius (manual-only): what a change breaks outside its diff. Every consumer of what the diff changed is listed (Python callers by AST, renamed keys, fields, columns, env vars and flags by literal name in every tracked text file), each gets a cited breaks, cleared or unknown verdict, and the change is called safe only when the one fact it is safe because of has a proof that passes on a copy of the change and fails on a copy with that fact broken; the answer states the level the helper saw, never one typed. And mistake-proof (manual-only): make a mistake agents keep repeating impossible. Candidates are mined from history (reverts, commits that bring a reverted change back, fixes naming an earlier commit, workaround comments) and from the operator's corrections; a class needs two pieces of evidence that exist, a fix level from architecture down to docs with a reason each stronger level did not work, and a check that fails on the commit where the mistake is and passes on the working tree, run in CI when the repo has CI; the agent file's rule table names what enforces each rule, and a docs-only rule that recurs is a repeat. And untangle (manual-only): untangle where the history says changes hurt. Files ranked by commits and fix commits, and pairs that keep changing together, each get a target or a reason to skip; the tests are recorded on the committed tree first and every test already red is classified env, stale or bug (with its file:line); every changed file serves a target, every move's guard passes now and fails on the committed tree, and no test that was green goes red. And cleanup (manual-only): clear what agents leave behind. Candidates are listed by file:line (leftover copies, litter, orphaned modules, dead and duplicate functions, unused imports, debug leftovers, commented-out code, swallowed errors, stubs, hard-coded answers, change-log comments); the tests and files are recorded before any change, done is refused while a test that passed fails, fewer tests run or a deleted file is still named somewhere, and each run's record lets the next one say what is new and what came back. And checkup (manual-only): how well a codebase is structured, and what to fix first. One report over the git-tracked files in eight sections (easy to find things, one change in one place, dependencies one way, deep modules, one way per job, logic apart from I/O, dead code, tests that can fail), each measured by the sibling helpers or said `not checked`; every finding is weighted by the commits and fix commits of its files, so a tangle nobody changes ranks below files that keep changing together; each top finding needs a cost citing a commit that touched it or a reason it is right, and the three fixes are the costed findings, highest weight first. And dependency-health (manual-only): what the dependencies owe. Known holes (OSV.dev or a given advisories file, direct and pulled in by others, with what pulls them in), end-of-life runtimes, lockfiles out of step with their manifest, packages nothing uses (and ones used without an import), exact pins with no reason; an ecosystem it could not check is listed as not checked, never healthy; done is refused while a high finding is neither fixed nor accepted with a reason and a date, a test that passed fails, fewer tests run or a manifest changed without its lockfile, and the record lets the next run say what is new and which acceptances are due again. And state-machines (manual-only): the state machines a codebase never declared. Every field set to a string or a flag in two or more places is listed with every write and check by file:line, a value checked but never set is marked; the map must account for every write, give every written value a state, and cover each never-set value and each state nothing leaves with a finding; each bug needs a test that fails on a copy of the tree as it was (not on an import error), a fixed bug's test must pass now and an open one's still fail; done is refused while a test that passed fails or fewer run, and each machine is drawn as a diagram. And test-diet (manual-only): tests shorter to read and faster to run, with nothing lost. Setup repeated across tests is listed with the calls each copy replays to reach its state, slow tests with their time and cause (a sleep, the network, a process), and tests that only check mocks; the suite, each test's time and which planted bugs in the app code the tests import it catches are recorded first; done is refused while a lead is neither handled nor kept with a reason, a handled repeat is still repeated, a handled slow test is not twice as fast, an app file changed, the tests fail, got longer or slower, or a planted bug the old tests caught is missed now. The install runs no hooks.
